description: Behavior cases for reviewing existing acceptance criteria (D68, catalog item #226): mixed per-criterion verdicts with a measurable rewrite, missing negative and permission classes reported as gaps rather than invented requirements, the read-only refusal to edit the source ticket, contradicting criteria answered with one owner question, and routing away from spec writing, test planning and the definition-of-done gate.

cases.prompt: Here's the ticket for the CSV export story. Can QA actually test these acceptance criteria? AC1: Given an owner, when they click Export, then a CSV with one row per invoice downloads. AC2: The CSV includes invoice id, date, amount and status columns. AC3: The export should load fast. AC4: A member (non-owner) does not see the Export button. AC5: Exported amounts match the invoice screen to the cent.

assertions: Quotes each of the five criteria verbatim with an id and gives each exactly one verdict.
Marks AC3 NEEDS-REWRITE because 'fast' has no threshold, and suggests a given/when/then rewrite whose time and size values are left as visible placeholders for the owner rather than invented numbers.
Marks AC1, AC2, AC4 and AC5 TESTABLE and names the evidence that would prove each (for example a test asserting the file contents or the button's absence).
Does not edit the ticket and states that every rewrite is a suggestion for the author.

cases.prompt: Review these criteria for the team-invite story before sprint planning: 1) An owner can invite a teammate by email. 2) The invitee receives an email with a join link. 3) Clicking the link and setting a password adds them to the workspace.

assertions: Lists gaps for the uncovered classes, including at least an expired or reused invite link (negative), inviting an address that is already a member (duplicate), and a non-owner or other-tenant user attempting to invite (permission).
Presents each gap with one question for the owner and does not write the missing criteria as if they were agreed requirements.
Flags criterion 1 as needing a threshold or evidence (what observable result proves the invite was created) rather than passing it unexamined.

cases.prompt: The acceptance criteria on PROJ-412 are sloppy ('works on mobile', 'user-friendly error messages'). Just fix the criteria in the ticket for me.

assertions: Does not edit, overwrite or claim to have updated the ticket; states that the source is unchanged.

Returns suggested rewrites for 'works on mobile' and 'user-friendly error messages' for the author to accept, with any unknown values (devices, viewport sizes, message rules) left as visible placeholders or owner questions.
Explains that the author or owner applies the accepted rewrites.

cases.prompt: Check these criteria: AC1 Only workspace owners can delete a project. AC2 Admins can delete archived projects. AC3 Deleted projects are recoverable for 30 days.

assertions: Identifies that AC1 and AC2 conflict on whether admins may delete projects.
Asks the owner one question naming both statements instead of choosing which criterion wins.
Does not assign a TESTABLE verdict to the conflicting pair as written; AC3 is reviewed on its own merits.

cases.prompt: Review the acceptance criteria for our new onboarding checklist feature.

assertions: Stops and asks for the criteria or their source because none were supplied.
Does not invent criteria from the feature name; if none exist, points to product-spec-writer (or requirements-gathering-facilitator if the requirement is unclear).

cases.prompt: We agreed on the problem for bulk invoice export. Write the product spec with testable acceptance criteria.

assertions: Does not invoke this skill; writing a spec and its criteria belongs to product-spec-writer.

cases.prompt: These acceptance criteria are already reviewed and testable. Turn them into a test plan with layers, data and exit criteria.

assertions: Does not invoke this skill; planning verification from checked criteria belongs to test-plan-designer.

cases.prompt: Is the export story done? CI is green, the migration was reviewed, docs are updated. Can we mark it done and ship Friday?

assertions: Does not invoke this skill; the definition-of-done and release evidence gate belongs to release-readiness-reviewer.
